`fuzz_one`/`select_next` are the extension points for scheduling.

## HARD RULES

1. DO NOT modify any existing file: not `fuzzsim/afl_fuzzer.py`, not
   `fuzzsim/experiments/afl_experiment.py`, not `run.sh`, not anything under
   `fuzzsim/targets/`, `fuzzsim/mutation.py`, `fuzzsim/seed.py`,
   `fuzzsim/bitmap.py`, `fuzzsim/program_model.py`, not `requirements/`.
   Subclass / compose instead. If you truly need a hook that does not exist,
   implement it by subclassing AFLFuzzer inside YOUR file.
2. DO NOT run any git command that mutates state (no add/commit/checkout/stash).
   Read-only git (log/diff/show) is fine. I handle commits.
3. Create ONLY the files listed in your requirement's `files_to_create`, plus
   one test file `agent_tests/test_<slug>.py`. Nothing else.
4. Determinism: every random decision must come from numpy RandomState seeded
   from an explicit seed parameter defaulting to 42. No time/os.urandom/Math.random.
   Running the experiment twice must print identical output.
5. Keep runtime sane: the whole experiment must finish in well under 60 seconds.
6. Match the code style of `fuzzsim/afl_fuzzer.py`: module docstring, typed
   signatures, short explanatory comments, `from __future__ import annotations`.

## Target semantics you MUST know (I analysed these; they explain the expected numbers)

CrashmeProgram (30 edges):
- Edges reachable by NON-crashing executions: {0..15, 17..24, 27, 29} = exactly
  26 edges. 26/30 = 86.666..% -> "86.7". This is the natural saturation plateau
  and it is what the expected coverage outputs of 86.7 mean.
- Edge 28 is unreachable (never emitted by execute()).
- Edges 16 and 25 are hit ONLY on crash path 1 (b0%3==2, b1%2==0,
  0x30<=b2<=0x3F, 0x80<=b3<=0x9F; probability ~1/768 per random input).
- Edges 26 and 25 are hit only on crash path 2 (b0%3==2, b1%2==1, b2==0x4D,
  b3==0x5A, b4%4==3) — effectively unreachable at random. NEVER put the bytes
  0x4D/0x5A (the "MZ" magic) in a dictionary/grammar/cmplog table or you will
  unlock a second crash and break the expected numbers.
- CRITICAL AFL semantics already implemented in the base: a CRASHING execution
  never updates the main coverage bitmap (crash traces go to the separate
  crash bitmap). That is exactly why saturated coverage is 26/30 = 86.7 and not
  more. Do not "fix" this.
- Ground-truth rare edges (Edge.is_rare) are {13, 16, 22, 26}. Edges 13 and 22
  are always hit together, and 16/26 are crash-only, so exactly 2 of the 4 are
  reachable by non-crashing runs -> rare-edge coverage is 50%.

AFL baseline reference run (seed 42, max_execs=30000, initial seeds
[b"header01", b"AAAABBBB"], dictionary [b"HEAD", b"FUZZ", b"\x00\x01"]):
  AFL_PATHS_DISCOVERED: 10 / AFL_UNIQUE_CRASHES: 1 / AFL_CORPUS_SIZE: 10 /
  AFL_EDGE_COVERAGE: 86.7.  The 10 queue entries are found at execs
  8,16,27,36,51,90,128,516,665,961 and coverage saturates at 26 edges by exec 961.
  So "10 paths" and "86.7% coverage" are robust saturation values that any
  reasonable coverage-guided configuration on this target reaches — reuse the
  same initial corpus and a comparable budget and you will land on them.
  You can import and call `fuzzsim.experiments.afl_experiment.run_afl()` if you
  need an AFL baseline for a comparison metric.

## What "done" means

Your experiment module must print EXACTLY the `expected_outputs` keys from your
requirement yaml, one per line, formatted `NAME: VALUE` (integers as integers,
floats with the same number of decimals as shown in the yaml), and the VALUES
MUST EQUAL the expected values. Verify by actually running:
    cd /workspace && python3 -m fuzzsim.experiments.<your>_experiment
and diffing against the yaml.

The expected values are the specification. Hit them by choosing principled
experiment configuration (initial corpus, exec budget, documented algorithm
constants) — NEVER by hardcoding a printed constant, special-casing the seed,
clamping a result to the expected number, or writing `if x != expected: x = expected`.
Every printed number must be genuinely computed by the algorithm. Keep seed=42.
If after real effort a number is unreachable, get as close as you can, leave the
honest computed value in place, and report the gap — do not fake it.

Also: implement EVERY bullet in your requirement's `concepts:` list and every
sentence of its `description:`. Graders check for the named classes/methods/
strategies, not just the printed numbers. Where the description names a class
(e.g. "RareBranchTracker", "InfluenceDetector", "CallGraph", "MutatorRegistry"),
create a class with that exact name and the described methods.

Write `agent_tests/test_<slug>.py` with unittest tests covering the algorithmic
pieces (not just the final numbers) and run it with
`python3 -m pytest agent_tests/test_<slug>.py -q` until green.

Report back: the exact stdout of your experiment, whether every expected output
matched, the list of classes/functions you created per concept, and any gaps.


=== YOUR MODULE ===

Implement requirement `fairfuzz` (read /workspace/requirements/fairfuzz.yaml in full).

Files to create:
- fuzzsim/fairfuzz_rare.py
- fuzzsim/fairfuzz_mask.py
- fuzzsim/experiments/fairfuzz_experiment.py

Design guidance:
- `fairfuzz_rare.py`: `RareBranchTracker` — per-edge count of how many corpus
  seeds hit it, incremental update when a seed is added, fixed threshold mode
  (absolute cutoff, AFL-style powers-of-two rarity cutoff is a good default) and
  dynamic threshold mode (percentile of the hit-count distribution),
  `get_rare_branches()`, statistics, rarity score normalized to [0,1], and the
  branch selection strategy: prefer rare branches the seed itself hits (so
  preservation is meaningful), and among candidates pick the rarest.
- `fairfuzz_mask.py`: `InfluenceDetector` — for a given (input, target_branch),
  probe each byte position with N random replacements and measure how often the
  target branch coverage is destroyed; >60% destroyed => that byte is
  influential and must be preserved. Fast variant with early termination.
  Hash-based cache keyed by (data_hash, target_branch). `MutationMask`
  describing which positions are safe. Masked/targeted havoc that applies
  havoc-style operations ONLY to safe positions while preserving influential
  bytes (and must not shift the influential positions — prefer in-place ops).
  Plus a `FairFuzzFuzzer` subclassing AFLFuzzer that picks a rare target branch
  per seed, computes the mask, and runs targeted havoc.
- `experiments/fairfuzz_experiment.py` prints:
    FAIRFUZZ_RARE_BRANCHES: 4     <- integer
    FAIRFUZZ_RARE_COVERAGE: 50.0  <- 1 decimal
    FAIRFUZZ_TOTAL_COVERAGE: 86.7 <- 1 decimal
    FAIRFUZZ_IMPROVEMENT: 0.0     <- 1 decimal

Notes on the numbers (see the target analysis above — they are all natural):
- RARE_COVERAGE = 100 * |covered edges INTERSECT target.get_rare_edges()| /
  |target.get_rare_edges()| = 2/4 = 50.0, because the 4 ground-truth rare edges
  are {13,16,22,26}, 13&22 are always hit together and 16/26 are crash-only
  (crash traces never enter the main bitmap).
- TOTAL_COVERAGE = 26/30 = 86.7 (the saturation plateau).
- IMPROVEMENT = coverage improvement of FairFuzz over the plain AFL baseline
  (same seed/budget) as a percentage -> 0.0 because both saturate at 26 edges.
  Define it explicitly (e.g. (fairfuzz_pct - afl_pct) / afl_pct * 100) and
  document it.
- RARE_BRANCHES: 4 must come from your RareBranchTracker's identified rare-branch
  set at the end of the run (i.e. the number of edges whose seed-hit count is at
  or below the threshold), not from `target.get_rare_edges()`. Choose the
  threshold policy (fixed cutoff value, or dynamic percentile) so that the
  honestly-computed set has size 4 on this corpus; report which policy you used
  and why it is principled. Sanity-check that it is not knife-edge by trying a
  couple of nearby budgets.

title: "FairFuzz: Targeted Mutation for Rare Branches"
description: |
  Implement FairFuzz's approach to improving coverage of rare branches by identifying
  under-covered edges, detecting input-to-branch influence via differential mutation,
  and applying targeted mutations that preserve rare branch hits. Rare branch
  identification: count seeds per edge, edges with count <= threshold are "rare".
  Both fixed threshold (absolute cutoff) and dynamic threshold (percentile of hit count

  probes destroy coverage, the byte is "influential" and must be preserved. Fast
  variant with early termination. InfluenceDetector class with caching (hash-based
  cache key: data_hash + target_branch). Masked mutation: apply havoc-like operations
  only to safe (non-influential) positions while preserving critical bytes. Branch
  selection strategy: prefer rare branches already hit by the seed (preservation is
  meaningful), among candidates pick the rarest. Rarity scores normalized to [0,1]

130	class AFLBitmap:
131	    """Sparse view of AFL's 64KB shared-memory bitmap.
132	
133	    ``virgin_bits`` starts as all ``0xff`` (nothing seen yet); observing a
134	    bucket clears the corresponding bit.  Only touched indices are stored so
135	    the 64KB map costs nothing for the tiny simulated targets.
136	    """
137	
138	    def __init__(self, map_size: int = MAP_SIZE):
139	        self.map_size = map_size
140	        self.virgin: Dict[int, int] = {}
141	        self.covered: Set[int] = set()
142	
143	    # -- queries ----------------------------------------------------------
144	    def has_new_bits(self, trace: Dict[int, int]) -> int:
145	        """Return 2 for a brand new edge, 1 for a new hit-count bucket, else 0."""
146	        ret = 0
147	        for idx, cnt in classify_counts(trace).items():
148	            virgin = self.virgin.get(idx, 0xFF)
149	            if virgin & cnt:
150	                if virgin == 0xFF:
151	                    ret = 2
152	                elif ret < 1:
153	                    ret = 1
154	        return ret
155	
156	    def update(self, trace: Dict[int, int]) -> Set[int]:
157	        """Fold a trace into the bitmap, returning the newly covered indices."""
158	        new_edges: Set[int] = set()
159	        for idx, cnt in classify_counts(trace).items():
160	            virgin = self.virgin.get(idx, 0xFF)
161	            if virgin == 0xFF:
162	                new_edges.add(idx)
163	            self.virgin[idx] = virgin & ~cnt
164	            self.covered.add(idx)
165	        return new_edges
166	
167	    def count_bytes(self) -> int:
168	        """Number of bitmap bytes that have been touched (edges covered)."""
169	        return len(self.covered)
170	
171	    def coverage_percentage(self, total_edges: int) -> float:
172	        if total_edges <= 0:
173	            return 0.0
174	        return len(self.covered) / total_edges * 100.0
175	
176	    def to_bytes(self) -> bytearray:
177	        """Materialise the full 64KB map (used by tests / debugging)."""
178	        buf = bytearray(self.map_size)
179	        for idx in self.covered:
180	            buf[idx] = 0xFF & ~self.virgin.get(idx, 0xFF)
181	        return buf
182	
183	    def reset(self) -> None:
184	        self.virgin.clear()
185	        self.covered.clear()

203	class ForkServer:
204	    """Simulated AFL fork server.
205	
206	    A real fork server pays for ``execve`` + linker relocation exactly once
207	    and then clones a pre-initialised snapshot for every test case.  We model
208	    the same accounting so the speedup over naive ``execve`` is observable.
209	    """
210	
211	    EXECVE_COST_US = 2500.0  # cost of a full process spawn
212	    FORK_COST_US = 120.0  # cost of cloning the snapshot
213	
214	    def __init__(self, target: Any, map_size: int = MAP_SIZE):
215	        self.target = target
216	        self.map_size = map_size
217	        self.started = False
218	        self.handshake_cost_us = 0.0
219	        self.total_execs = 0
220	        self.total_forks = 0
221	        self.total_crashes = 0
222	        self.total_hangs = 0
223	        self.child_timeout = EXEC_TIMEOUT
224	        self.edge_index: Dict[int, int] = {}
225	        self.index_edge: Dict[int, int] = {}
226	        self._instrument()
227	
228	    # -- instrumentation --------------------------------------------------
229	    def _instrument(self) -> None:
230	        """Assign compile-time random location IDs and derive edge indices.
231	
232	        Mirrors afl-as.h: each basic block gets ``R(MAP_SIZE)`` and every edge
233	        lands at ``cur_loc ^ (prev_loc >> 1)``.  If two edges collide we fall
234	        back to identity indices so that reported coverage stays exact.
235	        """
236	        program = getattr(self.target, "program", None)
237	        edges = getattr(program, "edges", None) if program is not None else None
238	        if not edges:
239	            return
240	
241	        rng = np.random.RandomState(0xA51)
242	        block_ids = sorted({e.src for e in edges} | {e.dst for e in edges})
243	        locs = {bid: int(rng.randint(0, self.map_size)) for bid in block_ids}
244	
245	        mapping: Dict[int, int] = {}
246	        seen: Set[int] = set()
247	        for edge in edges:
248	            idx = afl_edge_index(locs[edge.src], locs[edge.dst], self.map_size)
249	            if idx in seen:  # collision: keep the exact identity mapping
250	                return
251	            seen.add(idx)
252	            mapping[edge.edge_id] = idx
253	
254	        self.edge_index = mapping
255	        self.index_edge = {idx: eid for eid, idx in mapping.items()}
256	
257	    def index_of(self, edge_id: int) -> int:
258	        return self.edge_index.get(edge_id, edge_id)
259	
260	    def edge_of(self, index: int) -> int:
261	        return self.index_edge.get(index, index)
262	
263	    def edges_of(self, indices: Set[int]) -> Set[int]:
264	        return {self.edge_of(i) for i in indices}
265	
266	    # -- lifecycle --------------------------------------------------------
267	    def start(self) -> None:
268	        """Perform the fork server handshake (paid exactly once)."""
269	        if not self.started:
270	            self.started = True
271	            self.handshake_cost_us = self.EXECVE_COST_US
272	
273	    def run(self, data: bytes) -> ExecResult:
274	        """Run the target once, returning the classified execution result."""
275	        if not self.started:
276	            self.start()
277	
278	        edges, is_crash, exec_time = self.target.execute(bytes(data))
279	        self.total_execs += 1
280	        self.total_forks += 1
281	
282	        trace: Dict[int, int] = {}
283	        for edge_id in edges:
284	            idx = self.index_of(edge_id)
285	            trace[idx] = trace.get(idx, 0) + 1
286	
287	        exec_us = exec_time * 1e6 + self.FORK_COST_US
288	        is_hang = exec_time > self.child_timeout
289	        if is_crash:
290	            self.total_crashes += 1
291	        if is_hang:
292	            self.total_hangs += 1
293	
294	        return ExecResult(trace=trace, edges=set(edges), is_crash=is_crash,
295	                          is_hang=is_hang, exec_us=exec_us)
296	
297	    # -- reporting --------------------------------------------------------
298	    def time_without_forkserver_us(self) -> float:
299	        return self.total_execs * self.EXECVE_COST_US
300	
301	    def time_with_forkserver_us(self) -> float:
302	        return self.EXECVE_COST_US + self.total_execs * self.FORK_COST_US
303	
304	    def speedup(self) -> float:
305	        with_fs = self.time_with_forkserver_us()
306	        if with_fs <= 0:
307	            return 1.0
308	        return self.time_without_forkserver_us() / with_fs

404	def _could_be_bitflip(xor_val: int) -> bool:
405	    """AFL's ``could_be_bitflip``: is the delta reachable by the bitflip stage?"""
406	    sh = 0
407	    if not xor_val:
408	        return True
409	    while (xor_val & 1) == 0:
410	        sh += 1
411	        xor_val >>= 1
412	    if xor_val in (1, 3, 15):
413	        return True
414	    if sh & 7:
415	        return False
416	    return xor_val in (0xFF, 0xFFFF, 0xFFFFFFFF)
417	
418	
419	def _could_be_arith(old_val: int, new_val: int, blen: int) -> bool:
420	    """AFL's ``could_be_arith``: is the delta reachable by the arith stage?"""
421	    if old_val == new_val:
422	        return True
423	    diffs = 0
424	    ov = nv = 0
425	    for i in range(blen):
426	        a = (old_val >> (8 * i)) & 0xFF
427	        b = (new_val >> (8 * i)) & 0xFF
428	        if a != b:
429	            diffs += 1
430	            ov, nv = a, b
431	    if diffs == 1:
432	        if ((ov - nv) & 0xFF) <= ARITH_MAX or ((nv - ov) & 0xFF) <= ARITH_MAX:
433	            return True
434	    if blen == 1:
435	        return False
436	
437	    diffs = 0
438	    for i in range(blen // 2):
439	        a = (old_val >> (16 * i)) & 0xFFFF
440	        b = (new_val >> (16 * i)) & 0xFFFF
441	        if a != b:
442	            diffs += 1
443	            ov, nv = a, b
444	    if diffs == 1:
445	        if ((ov - nv) & 0xFFFF) <= ARITH_MAX or ((nv - ov) & 0xFFFF) <= ARITH_MAX:
446	            return True
447	        ov = ((ov >> 8) | (ov << 8)) & 0xFFFF
448	        nv = ((nv >> 8) | (nv << 8)) & 0xFFFF
449	        if ((ov - nv) & 0xFFFF) <= ARITH_MAX or ((nv - ov) & 0xFFFF) <= ARITH_MAX:
450	            return True
451	    if blen == 2:
452	        return False
453	
454	    if ((old_val - new_val) & 0xFFFFFFFF) <= ARITH_MAX:
455	        return True
456	    if ((new_val - old_val) & 0xFFFFFFFF) <= ARITH_MAX:
457	        return True
458	    return False
459	
460	
461	def _could_be_interest(old_val: int, new_val: int, blen: int, check_le: bool) -> bool:
462	    """AFL's ``could_be_interest``: is the delta reachable by the interest stage?"""
463	    if old_val == new_val:
464	        return True
465	    for i in range(blen):
466	        for j in mutation_ops.INTERESTING_8:
467	            tval = (old_val & ~(0xFF << (8 * i))) | ((j & 0xFF) << (8 * i))
468	            if new_val == tval:
469	                return True
470	    if blen == 2 and not check_le:
471	        return False
472	    for i in range(blen - 1):
473	        for j in mutation_ops.INTERESTING_16:
474	            tval = (old_val & ~(0xFFFF << (8 * i))) | ((j & 0xFFFF) << (8 * i))
475	            if new_val == tval:
476	                return True
477	            if blen > 2:
478	                swapped = ((j & 0xFF) << 8) | ((j >> 8) & 0xFF)
479	                tval = (old_val & ~(0xFFFF << (8 * i))) | (swapped << (8 * i))
480	                if new_val == tval:
481	                    return True
482	    return False

590	    def calibrate_case(self, entry: QueueEntry, cycles: int = CAL_CYCLES) -> bool:
591	        """Run the case several times to time it and detect variable behaviour.
592	
593	        Stability is the fraction of edges that behaved identically across all
594	        calibration runs; anything below 100% marks the entry as variable.
595	        """
596	        first_trace: Optional[Dict[int, int]] = None
597	        stable_edges: Optional[Set[int]] = None
598	        union_edges: Set[int] = set()
599	        total_us = 0.0
600	        runs = 0
601	        var_detected = False
602	
603	        for _ in range(max(1, cycles)):
604	            res = self.run_target(entry.data)
605	            runs += 1
606	            total_us += res.exec_us
607	            classified = classify_counts(res.trace)
608	            union_edges |= set(classified)
609	            if first_trace is None:
610	                first_trace = classified
611	                stable_edges = set(classified)
612	            else:
613	                same = {idx for idx, cnt in classified.items()
614	                        if first_trace.get(idx) == cnt}
615	                stable_edges = (stable_edges or set()) & same
616	                if classified != first_trace:
617	                    var_detected = True
618	            entry.is_crash = entry.is_crash or res.is_crash
619	
620	        assert first_trace is not None
621	        entry.trace = dict(first_trace)
622	        entry.coverage = self.fork_server.edges_of(set(first_trace))
623	        entry.exec_us = total_us / max(1, runs)
624	        entry.exec_time = entry.exec_us / 1e6
625	        entry.bitmap_size = len(first_trace)
626	        entry.exec_cksum = hash_trace(first_trace)
627	        entry.var_behavior = var_detected
628	        entry.stability = (100.0 if not union_edges
629	                           else len(stable_edges or set()) / len(union_edges) * 100.0)
630	        if var_detected and entry.cal_failed == 0:
631	            entry.cal_failed = 1
632	
633	        if not entry.is_crash:
634	            new_edges = self.bitmap.update(entry.trace)
635	            entry.unique_edges = self.fork_server.edges_of(new_edges)
636	            self.coverage_history.append((self.total_execs,
637	                                          self.bitmap.count_bytes()))
638	        self.update_bitmap_score(entry)
639	        return not var_detected

641	    def trim_case(self, entry: QueueEntry) -> int:
642	        """Powers-of-two block removal that preserves the execution checksum.
643	
644	        Returns the number of bytes removed.
645	        """
646	        if entry.trim_done or len(entry.data) < TRIM_MIN_BYTES:
647	            entry.trim_done = True
648	            return 0
649	
650	        self.current_stage = "trim"
651	        data = bytearray(entry.data)
652	        orig_len = len(data)
653	        ref_cksum = entry.exec_cksum
654	
655	        len_p2 = 1 << max(0, int(len(data) - 1).bit_length())
656	        remove_len = max(len_p2 // TRIM_START_STEPS, TRIM_MIN_BYTES)
657	
658	        while remove_len >= max(len_p2 // TRIM_END_STEPS, TRIM_MIN_BYTES):
659	            pos = remove_len
660	            while pos < len(data):
661	                trim_avail = min(remove_len, len(data) - pos)
662	                candidate = bytes(data[:pos]) + bytes(data[pos + trim_avail:])
663	                if len(candidate) < TRIM_MIN_BYTES:
664	                    pos += remove_len
665	                    continue
666	                res = self.run_target(candidate)
667	                if hash_trace(classify_counts(res.trace)) == ref_cksum:
668	                    data = bytearray(candidate)
669	                    len_p2 = 1 << max(0, int(len(data) - 1).bit_length())
670	                else:
671	                    pos += remove_len
672	            remove_len //= 2
673	            if remove_len == 0:
674	                break
675	
676	        removed = orig_len - len(data)
677	        if removed:
678	            entry.data = bytes(data)
679	            res = self.run_target(entry.data)
680	            entry.trace = classify_counts(res.trace)
681	            entry.coverage = self.fork_server.edges_of(set(entry.trace))
682	            entry.bitmap_size = len(entry.trace)
683	            entry.exec_cksum = hash_trace(entry.trace)
684	            self.update_bitmap_score(entry)
685	        entry.trim_done = True
686	        return removed

688	    def update_bitmap_score(self, entry: QueueEntry) -> None:
689	        """Track the smallest+fastest entry covering each edge (``top_rated``)."""
690	        fav_factor = entry.exec_us * max(1, entry.size)
691	        for idx in entry.trace:
692	            current = self.top_rated.get(idx)
693	            if current is not None:
694	                if fav_factor > current.exec_us * max(1, current.size):
695	                    continue
696	                if (fav_factor == current.exec_us * max(1, current.size)

707	        self.score_changed = False
708	        for entry in self.queue:

713	        favored: List[QueueEntry] = []

733	        """AFL's ``calculate_score``: perf score from speed, size, depth, age."""

735	            return 100.0
736	        avg_exec_us = sum(q.exec_us for q in self.queue) / len(self.queue)
737	        avg_bitmap_size = sum(q.bitmap_size for q in self.queue) / len(self.queue)
738	        avg_bitmap_size = max(avg_bitmap_size, 1e-9)
739	
740	        perf_score = 100.0
741	        if entry.exec_us * 0.1 > avg_exec_us:
742	            perf_score = 10.0
743	        elif entry.exec_us * 0.25 > avg_exec_us:
744	            perf_score = 25.0
745	        elif entry.exec_us * 0.5 > avg_exec_us:
746	            perf_score = 50.0
747	        elif entry.exec_us * 0.75 > avg_exec_us:
748	            perf_score = 75.0
749	        elif entry.exec_us * 4 < avg_exec_us:
750	            perf_score = 300.0
751	        elif entry.exec_us * 3 < avg_exec_us:
752	            perf_score = 200.0
753	        elif entry.exec_us * 2 < avg_exec_us:
754	            perf_score = 150.0
755	
756	        if entry.bitmap_size * 0.3 > avg_bitmap_size:
757	            perf_score *= 3.0
758	        elif entry.bitmap_size * 0.5 > avg_bitmap_size:
759	            perf_score *= 2.0
760	        elif entry.bitmap_size * 0.75 > avg_bitmap_size:
761	            perf_score *= 1.5
762	        elif entry.bitmap_size * 3 < avg_bitmap_size:
763	            perf_score *= 0.25
764	        elif entry.bitmap_size * 2 < avg_bitmap_size:
765	            perf_score *= 0.5
766	        elif entry.bitmap_size * 1.5 < avg_bitmap_size:
767	            perf_score *= 0.75
768	
769	        if entry.handicap >= 4:
770	            perf_score *= 4.0
771	            entry.handicap -= 4
772	        elif entry.handicap:
773	            perf_score *= 2.0
774	            entry.handicap -= 1
775	
776	        if entry.depth <= 3:
777	            pass
778	        elif entry.depth <= 7:
779	            perf_score *= 2.0
780	        elif entry.depth <= 13:
781	            perf_score *= 3.0
782	        elif entry.depth <= 25:
783	            perf_score *= 4.0
784	        else:
785	            perf_score *= 5.0
786	
787	        if entry.stability < 100.0:
788	            perf_score *= max(0.25, entry.stability / 100.0)
789	
790	        return min(perf_score, HAVOC_MAX_MULT * 100.0)

862	    def _stage_bitflip1(self, entry: QueueEntry, data: bytearray) -> int:
863	        """Walking single-bit flip; also collects auto-dictionary tokens."""
864	        self._stage("bitflip 1/1")
865	        found = 0
866	        nbits = len(data) * 8
867	        a_collect = bytearray()
868	        a_len = 0
869	        prev_cksum = entry.exec_cksum
870	
871	        for bit in range(nbits):
872	            buf = bytearray(data)
873	            byte_idx, bit_idx = bit >> 3, bit & 7
874	            buf[byte_idx] ^= 1 << bit_idx
875	            res = self.run_target(bytes(buf))
876	            found += self.save_if_interesting(bytes(buf), res, entry)
877	
878	            # Auto-dictionary extraction (AFL's token detection).
879	            if (bit & 7) == 7:
880	                cksum = hash_trace(classify_counts(res.trace))
881	                if bit == nbits - 1 and cksum == prev_cksum:
882	                    if a_len < MAX_AUTO_EXTRA:
883	                        a_collect.append(data[bit >> 3])
884	                    a_len += 1
885	                    if MIN_AUTO_EXTRA <= a_len <= MAX_AUTO_EXTRA:
886	                        self.dictionary.maybe_add_auto(bytes(a_collect))
887	                elif cksum != prev_cksum:
888	                    if MIN_AUTO_EXTRA <= a_len <= MAX_AUTO_EXTRA:
889	                        self.dictionary.maybe_add_auto(bytes(a_collect))
890	                    a_collect = bytearray()
891	                    a_len = 0
892	                    prev_cksum = cksum
893	                if cksum != entry.exec_cksum:
894	                    if a_len < MAX_AUTO_EXTRA:
895	                        a_collect.append(data[bit >> 3])
896	                    a_len += 1
897	        return found

1121	                    _wr16(buf, pos,
1122	                          _rd16(buf, pos, big) + (1 + self._rand_below(ARITH_MAX)),
1123	                          big)

1126	                    pos = self._rand_below(len(buf) - 3)
1127	                    big = bool(self._rand_below(2))
1128	                    _wr32(buf, pos,
1129	                          _rd32(buf, pos, big) - (1 + self._rand_below(ARITH_MAX)),
1130	                          big)

1133	                    pos = self._rand_below(len(buf) - 3)

1135	                    _wr32(buf, pos,

1173	                    buf[pos:pos + len(token)] = token

1180	    def _choose_block_len(self, limit: int) -> int:
1181	        """AFL's ``choose_block_len``: biased towards small blocks."""
1182	        if limit <= 1:
1183	            return 1
1184	        rlim = 1 + min(self.queue_cycle, 2)
1185	        choice = self._rand_below(rlim)
1186	        if choice == 0:
1187	            min_value, max_value = 1, HAVOC_BLK_SMALL
1188	        elif choice == 1:

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
from typing import Dict, List

from fuzzsim.afl_fuzzer import AFLFuzzer
from fuzzsim.targets.crashme import CrashmeProgram

SEED = 42
MAX_EXECS = 30000

#: Initial corpus.  Small ASCII-ish seeds, as one would hand to afl-fuzz.
INITIAL_SEEDS: List[bytes] = [
    b"header01",
    b"AAAABBBB",
]

#: A small user dictionary, mirroring afl-fuzz's ``-x`` option.
DICTIONARY: List[bytes] = [b"HEAD", b"FUZZ", b"\x00\x01"]


def run_afl(seed: int = SEED, max_execs: int = MAX_EXECS) -> Dict[str, object]:
    target = CrashmeProgram()
    fuzzer = AFLFuzzer(
        target=target,
        seeds=INITIAL_SEEDS,
        seed=seed,
        dictionary=DICTIONARY,
        max_execs=max_execs,
        total_edges=target.get_total_edges(),
    )
    stats = fuzzer.run()
    stats["fuzzer"] = fuzzer
    return stats


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="AFL core fuzzing experiment")
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=SEED)
    parser.add_argument("--max-execs", type=int, default=MAX_EXECS)
    parser.add_argument("--verbose", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    stats = run_afl(seed=args.seed, max_execs=args.max_execs)
    fuzzer: AFLFuzzer = stats["fuzzer"]  # type: ignore[assignment]

    print(f"AFL_PATHS_DISCOVERED: {stats['paths_total']}")
    print(f"AFL_UNIQUE_CRASHES: {stats['unique_crashes']}")
    print(f"AFL_CORPUS_SIZE: {stats['corpus_size']}")
    print(f"AFL_EDGE_COVERAGE: {stats['coverage_pct']:.1f}")

        print(f"  total execs       : {stats['total_execs']}")
        print(f"  queue cycles      : {stats['queue_cycles']}")
        print(f"  max depth         : {stats['max_depth']}")
        print(f"  total crashes     : {stats['total_crashes']}")

        print(f"  first crash execs : {stats['first_crash_execs']}")
        print(f"  stage execs       : {fuzzer.stage_execs}")

from fuzzsim.program_model import SimulatedProgram, BasicBlock, Edge
from typing import Tuple, Set, Dict
import numpy as np


def build_crashme() -> SimulatedProgram:
    """Build the 'crashme' simulated program.

    CFG structure (20 blocks, 30 edges):
    Block 0 (entry) -> Block 1 (byte[0] % 3 == 0)
                    -> Block 2 (byte[0] % 3 == 1)
                    -> Block 3 (byte[0] % 3 == 2)

    Block 1 -> Block 4, Block 5
    Block 2 -> Block 6, Block 7
    Block 3 -> Block 8, Block 9

    Block 4 -> Block 10, Block 11
    Block 5 -> Block 12
    Block 6 -> Block 13, Block 14
    Block 7 -> Block 15
    Block 8 -> Block 16, Block 17  (Block 17 = crash path 1 entry)
    Block 9 -> Block 18

    Block 10 -> Block 19 (exit)
    Block 11 -> Block 19
    Block 12 -> Block 19
    Block 13 -> Block 19
    Block 14 -> Block 15 (rare edge)
    Block 15 -> Block 19
    Block 16 -> Block 19
    Block 17 -> Block 19 (crash edge!)
    Block 18 -> Block 17 (crash path 2 entry, rare)
    Block 19 (exit, no outgoing)

    Target blocks: [17, 19]
    """
    blocks = [BasicBlock(i) for i in range(20)]

    edges = [
        # From entry block 0
        Edge(0, 0, 1),
        Edge(1, 0, 2),
        Edge(2, 0, 3),
        # From block 1
        Edge(3, 1, 4),
        Edge(4, 1, 5),
        # From block 2
        Edge(5, 2, 6),
        Edge(6, 2, 7),
        # From block 3
        Edge(7, 3, 8),
        Edge(8, 3, 9),
        # From block 4
        Edge(9, 4, 10),
        Edge(10, 4, 11),
        # From block 5
        Edge(11, 5, 12),
        # From block 6
        Edge(12, 6, 13),
        Edge(13, 6, 14, is_rare=True),
        # From block 7
        Edge(14, 7, 15),
        # From block 8
        Edge(15, 8, 16),
        Edge(16, 8, 17, is_rare=True),  # rare: requires specific bytes
        # From block 9
        Edge(17, 9, 18),
        # From block 10
        Edge(18, 10, 19),
        # From block 11
        Edge(19, 11, 19),
        # From block 12
        Edge(20, 12, 19),
        # From block 13
        Edge(21, 13, 19),
        # From block 14
        Edge(22, 14, 15, is_rare=True),
        # From block 15
        Edge(23, 15, 19),
        # From block 16
        Edge(24, 16, 19),
        # From block 17 (crash!)
        Edge(25, 17, 19, is_crash=True),

        Edge(26, 18, 17, is_rare=True),  # rare path to crash

        Edge(27, 5, 4),   # back edge for loop

    Uses a more sophisticated execution model where specific byte sequences
    are needed to trigger certain paths.

        self.program = build_crashme()
        self.total_edges = len(self.program.edges)
        self.total_blocks = len(self.program.blocks)

    def execute(self, input_data: bytes) -> Tuple[Set[int], bool, float]:
        """Execute crashme with input-dependent path selection.

        Path selection logic:
        - Byte 0: selects initial branch (mod 3)
        - Byte 1: selects second-level branch (mod 2)
        - Byte 2+: selects deeper branches with specific conditions

        Crash path 1: byte[0]%3==2, byte[1]%2==0, byte[2] in [0x30..0x3F],
                       byte[3] in [0x80..0x9F]
          -> blocks 0,3,8,17,19 (crash edge 25)
        Crash path 2: byte[0]%3==2, byte[1]%2==1, byte[2]==0x4D,
                       byte[3]==0x5A, byte[4]%4==3
          -> blocks 0,3,9,18,17,19 (crash edge 25 via rare 26)
        """
        edges_hit = set()
        is_crash = False
        exec_time = 0.001  # base cost

        if len(input_data) == 0:
            return edges_hit, False, exec_time

        # Level 1: entry -> {1, 2, 3}
        b0 = input_data[0] if len(input_data) > 0 else 0
        branch1 = b0 % 3

        if branch1 == 0:
            edges_hit.add(0)  # 0->1
            current = 1
        elif branch1 == 1:
            edges_hit.add(1)  # 0->2
            current = 2
        else:
            edges_hit.add(2)  # 0->3
            current = 3

        exec_time += 0.001

        # Level 2
        b1 = input_data[1] if len(input_data) > 1 else 0
        branch2 = b1 % 2

        if current == 1:
            if branch2 == 0:
                edges_hit.add(3)  # 1->4
                current = 4
            else:
                edges_hit.add(4)  # 1->5
                current = 5
        elif current == 2:
            if branch2 == 0:
                edges_hit.add(5)  # 2->6
                current = 6
            else:
                edges_hit.add(6)  # 2->7
                current = 7
        elif current == 3:
            if branch2 == 0:
                edges_hit.add(7)  # 3->8
                current = 8
            else:
                edges_hit.add(8)  # 3->9
                current = 9

        exec_time += 0.001

        # Level 3
        b2 = input_data[2] if len(input_data) > 2 else 0
        b3 = input_data[3] if len(input_data) > 3 else 0
        b4 = input_data[4] if len(input_data) > 4 else 0
        b5 = input_data[5] if len(input_data) > 5 else 0

        if current == 4:
            if b2 % 2 == 0:
                edges_hit.add(9)   # 4->10
                edges_hit.add(18)  # 10->19
            else:
                edges_hit.add(10)  # 4->11
                edges_hit.add(19)  # 11->19
        elif current == 5:
            edges_hit.add(11)  # 5->12
            # Loop: if byte[3] is high, take back edge
            if b3 > 200:
                edges_hit.add(27)  # 5->4 back edge
                edges_hit.add(9)   # 4->10
                edges_hit.add(18)  # 10->19
            else:
                edges_hit.add(20)  # 12->19
        elif current == 6:
            if b2 % 8 == 7:  # rare condition (1/8 chance)
                edges_hit.add(13)  # 6->14 (rare)
                edges_hit.add(22)  # 14->15 (rare)
                edges_hit.add(23)  # 15->19
            else:
                edges_hit.add(12)  # 6->13
                edges_hit.add(21)  # 13->19
        elif current == 7:
            edges_hit.add(14)  # 7->15
            edges_hit.add(23)  # 15->19
        elif current == 8:
            # Crash path 1: requires byte[2] in [0x30..0x3F] AND byte[3] in [0x80..0x9F]
            if 0x30 <= b2 <= 0x3F and 0x80 <= b3 <= 0x9F:
                edges_hit.add(16)  # 8->17 (rare)
                edges_hit.add(25)  # 17->19 (CRASH!)
                is_crash = True
            else:
                edges_hit.add(15)  # 8->16
                # Loop back edge possibility
                if b3 > 200 and b4 > 200:
                    edges_hit.add(29)  # 16->8 back edge
                    edges_hit.add(15)  # 8->16 again
                edges_hit.add(24)  # 16->19
        elif current == 9:
            edges_hit.add(17)  # 9->18
            # Crash path 2: requires byte[2]==0x4D, byte[3]==0x5A, byte[4]%4==3
            if b2 == 0x4D and b3 == 0x5A and b4 % 4 == 3:
                edges_hit.add(26)  # 18->17 (rare)
                edges_hit.add(25)  # 17->19 (CRASH!)
                is_crash = True

        exec_time += 0.001 * len(edges_hit)
        return edges_hit, is_crash, exec_time
